competitions.result: Fifth round — lost 1–0 to Everton in the second replay.
Third round — lost 3–1 away to Manchester United.

in.note: Permanent signing in June 1990 after the previous season’s loan.

overview: Liverpool won their opening eight league matches but finished second in the First Division, seven points behind Arsenal. Kenny Dalglish resigned on 22 February 1991, two days after a 4–4 FA Cup replay against Everton. Ronnie Moran took temporary charge before Graeme Souness returned from Rangers as manager in April.

Ian Rush led the scoring with 26 competitive goals. Ronny Rosenthal’s loan became a permanent move, while January arrivals included Jamie Redknapp from Bournemouth and David Speedie from Coventry City. Liverpool shared the Charity Shield with Manchester United after a 1–1 draw, but United later won their League Cup third-round tie 3–1.

Everton ended Liverpool’s FA Cup run by winning the second replay 1–0 at Goodison Park. Moran’s spell included a 7–1 league win at Derby County and a 5–4 victory at Leeds United. Liverpool finished the season with 76 points, scoring 77 league goals and conceding 40.

sources.label: Liverpool FC: Kenny Dalglish, first spell
sources.claims: 1989–90 brought the 18th league title; resignation two days after the 20 February 1991 Everton replay. The profile’s claim of ten opening league wins in 1990–91 is not used: fixtures show eight league wins and two League Cup wins.

sources.label: Liverpool FC: Graeme Souness, manager
sources.claims: Managed from 1991 to 1994; successive sixth places, 1992 FA Cup win, heart surgery and Moran’s cover, departure after the Bristol City cup defeat. Transfer dates come from the ledgers.

sources.label: Liverpool FC: Ronnie Moran
sources.claims: Caretaker after Dalglish’s 1991 resignation and during Souness’s recovery from heart surgery in 1992.

sources.label: LFChistory: managerial appointments

sources.label: Liverpool FC: Ronny Rosenthal
sources.claims: Initially loaned from Standard Liege in spring 1990, followed by a permanent summer move; seven goals in the title run-in. Also corroborates eight opening league wins in 1990–91. The header’s playing years are not used as a departure date.

researchNotes: Overview evidence: paragraph 1 — lfch-games, rsssf-league, lfc-dalglish, lfc-moran, lfc-souness and lfch-manager-dates; paragraph 2 — lfch-scorers, afv-scorer, lfch-transfers, lfc-shield and lfch-games; paragraph 3 — lfch-games, lfch-manager-dates and rsssf-league.

The official Dalglish profile says ten straight opening league wins. The fixture list gives eight, plus two League Cup victories; the official Rosenthal profile independently confirms eight. The erroneous ten-league-win claim is excluded.

Arsenal’s 83 points already include their two-point deduction. The final gap is seven. Moran’s caretaker spell is included explicitly. Redknapp is a signing, not a key player before his first-team debut.
managerNote: Dalglish resigned in February 1991. Moran served as caretaker before Souness was appointed on 16 April.
